key_insight: Performance-weighted SHAP aggregation can summarize which factors matter most in COVID-19 mortality models while also showing that feature importance is not equally stable across algorithms or retraining runs.
clinical_relevance: For clinical AI interpretation, this suggests that both attribution magnitude and attribution consistency should be checked before relying on model explanations in practice.
method: Prospective cohort of 1,857 hospitalized COVID-19 patients from two hospitals in Peru.
Compared 10 predictive algorithms with five-fold cross-validation and weighted SHAP attributions by mean AUROC.
Assessed feature-importance variability across 30 resampled training trials and patient-level alignment with cosine similarity.
evidence_signal: Random forest had the highest mean AUROC (0.925), and attribution profiles were much more similar within the same algorithm across retraining than across different algorithms in the same trial.
watch_item: SHAP rankings were averaged and normalized across resamples, so the most important features may still vary by model choice, training split, and cohort context.
paper_title: Ensemble SHAP Aggregation and Attribution Variability in Clinical Machine Learning: A COVID-19 Mortality Study
